Text:
# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH L. MONOCYTOGENES

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible after obtaining blood cultures and performing a lumbar puncture to obtain cerebrospinal fluid.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for a total duration of 21 days. If gentamicin is added for synergy, treat for at least 1 week. May be extended for up to 3 weeks in those who are poor responders and do not have signs of toxicity.

---

Therapy:
Preferred:

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R for 21 days

< OPTIONAL ADD ON TO ONE OF THE AGENTS ABOVE FOR SYNERGY >
Gentamicin 2 mg/kg IV x 1 then 1.7 mg/kg IV q8h ($) R,O for 7 days

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q6h ($$$) R,DI

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Inpatient):*
Van de Beek et al., Clin Microbiol Infect, 2016, 22.S37-S62
